summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Antioquia (incl. Medellín and Bello): by a wide margin the country's most lethal department for LGBTIQ people. Regional evidence: 45 of the 270 LGBTIQ+ killings recorded nationally in 2025 occurred here; the director of Caribe Afirmativo presented the department as one of the most dangerous for LGBTIQ+ people in the country; reporting covering part of the year states that more than half of the country's murders of this population took place in the department, three of them in the municipality of Bello. Emblematic case: Sara Millerey González Borja, 32, a trans woman, beaten and thrown into a creek in Bello on 4 April 2025 while onlookers filmed her; she died of her injuries, triggering vigils and a national alert about rising transfeminicides. No institutional protection finding for Antioquia appears in the monitoring reports - the framing is prejudice, violence and impunity. Scored relative to the national score (0.52) for Colombia.

sources.summary: El País in English (April 14, 2025): on the transphobic murder that shocked Colombia - Sara Millerey, 32, a trans woman, beaten in Bello, Antioquia on 4 April 2025 and thrown into a creek where onlookers filmed her drowning; she died of her injuries; the case was the third LGBTQ murder in Bello that year (the first two victims were gay men); national context: 13 trans people killed in the first quarter of 2025, presidential call to investigate, protests in several cities.

NOTE: not retrievable at fetch time (the CNN page returned only ad-feedback widgets); the underlying article covers attacks against LGBTQ people in Colombia in the context of the Sara Millerey case (per URL slug, Aug 6 2025).

The Guardian (July 30, 2024): 'We are killed for what we are' - trans women in Colombia targeted by armed groups; more than 40 transgender women killed in 2023 (41 recorded), eight between February and April 2024; in Caqueta armed groups circulated flyers announcing a 'social cleansing' against trans women, with remnants of the former largest rebel group still operating despite the 2016 peace agreement; national armed-group threat context.
